edges.description: Caveolae flatten under membrane tension and so act as a membrane reservoir; without them the sarcolemma cannot buffer stretch.
edges.source: Failure of Caveolar Invagination in Muscle

edges.description: Mechanical load during exercise injures fibers that cannot buffer membrane tension.
Repeated load-induced fiber damage is the proposed basis of the human myopathy. This rests on the mouse model; patient muscle pathology has not been compared with it in a citable source.
Sarcolemmal damage and fiber necrosis would release creatine kinase into the circulation. Inferred from the mechanism; the cited mouse study did not report serum creatine kinase.
Fibers injured by mechanical load would limit sustained exertion. Inferred from the exercise dependence of the mouse pathology.
Severe loss of deep caveolae in skeletal and cardiac muscle with preserved caveolin-3 and cavin-1.
edges.limitations: No patient muscle electron microscopy is available in a citable source, so whether patients lose caveolae to the same degree is unknown.
edges.target: Failure of Caveolar Invagination in Muscle

edges.description: Necrosis, inflammation and fiber-size variation appear after forced exercise; untrained mice are only mildly affected.
edges.limitations: The mouse phenotype needs a training protocol to appear, whereas the human disease presents in childhood without a stated exercise trigger; serum creatine kinase was not reported in the mouse.

nodes.description: HyperCKemia, named in the title of the published report.
Exercise intolerance with early fatigue, recorded in the Disease Ontology definition of the disease.

After physical exercise, syndapin III knockout skeletal muscle shows a widened fiber caliber spectrum, detached nuclei, necrotic fibers invaded by immune cells and secondary inflammation. Untrained knockout muscle shows only a mildly extended caliber spectrum.

evidence.reference_title: Deciphering caveolar functions by syndapin III KO-mediated impairment of caveolar invagination.
evidence.snippet: Under physical exercise, failure to invaginate caveolae using the membrane-shaping protein syndapin III coincided with a widened caliber spectrum, detached nuclei and signs of inflammation and necrosis.

evidence.reference_title: Deciphering caveolar functions by syndapin III KO-mediated impairment of caveolar invagination.
evidence.snippet: H&E stainings of musculus gastrocnemius cryosections from syndapin III KO mice subjected to physical exercise showed necrotic fibers invaded by immune cells as well as inflammation secondary to degeneration (Figure 11c–f; asterisk in Figure 11c).

evidence.reference_title: Deciphering caveolar functions by syndapin III KO-mediated impairment of caveolar invagination.
evidence.snippet: The muscle fibers of untrained syndapin III KO mice displayed an extended caliber spectrum being a sign of impaired muscle integrity.

nodes.description: Skeletal and cardiac muscle cells lacking syndapin III have severely reduced deep caveolae although caveolin-3 and cavin-1 levels at the plasma membrane are not reduced, so the coat proteins alone cannot form caveolae. Syndapin III sits at the caveolar neck, where membrane curvature changes.

evidence.snippet: Yet, different from other mouse models, the levels of the plasma membrane-associated caveolar coat proteins caveolin3 and cavin1 were both not reduced upon syndapin III KO.

nodes.description: Syndapin III knockout muscle cells are more easily damaged when membrane tension rises, shown by increased trypan blue uptake after hypo-osmotic swelling.

evidence.reference_title: Deciphering caveolar functions by syndapin III KO-mediated impairment of caveolar invagination.
evidence.snippet: (i–o) Trypan Blue assays with WT (i–k) and syndapin III KO cardiomyocytes (l–n) subjected to membrane tensions mimicked by mild hypoosmotic stress (5 min hypo30; j,m) and stronger hypoosmotic stress (5 min hypo15; k,n) unveiling a higher vulnerability of syndapin III KO cells under conditions increasing membrane tensions.

nodes.description: Biallelic truncating PACSIN3 variants are expected to remove syndapin III, whose F-BAR domain binds lipid membranes and bends them into tubules about 80 nm in diameter, matching the curvature of caveolae. A truncated N-terminal fragment retaining only the first 70 residues has none of these F-BAR functions.
